Meaning in plain words: A shared framework of method, content and guidance for designing and governing enterprise architecture.
How this template applies it: This template is structured around it: chapters follow the ADM and registers follow the content framework.

Core concept (chapter 3): What is Architecture in the Context of the TOGAF Standard?
Meaning in plain words: Architecture means both the structure of an enterprise or system and the description of that structure over time.
How this template applies it: Every chapter describes structure (what is) and a plan for change (what will be).

Core concept (chapter 3): What Kind of Architecture Does the TOGAF Standard Deal With?
Meaning in plain words: Four architecture domains: business, data, application and technology, plus the content that describes them.
How this template applies it: Chapters 10 to 13 hold the four domains; chapter 2 adds eight more streams.

Meaning in plain words: A repeatable cycle from vision to governance, with requirements management at the centre.
How this template applies it: Chapter 15 and the lifecycle diagram show the ADM applied; the crosswalk ties gates to phases.

Meaning in plain words: The set of services an architecture team offers the organisation, from support to planning to practice building.
How this template applies it: Chapter 1 lists each service with the template artefact that delivers it.

Meaning in plain words: Services that keep the enterprise aligned: strategy support, standards, reuse and portfolio advice.
How this template applies it: Principles, standards and decision records supply this service.

Meaning in plain words: Services that help projects design solutions that fit the architecture.
How this template applies it: Component catalogue, patterns and building blocks are the design support kit.

Meaning in plain words: Services that guide build teams: standards, reviews and compliance checks.
How this template applies it: Quality gates, definition of ready and done, and the QA checklist.

Meaning in plain words: Services that draw out, structure and validate what stakeholders need.
How this template applies it: The BABOK approach, requirements register and stakeholder analysis.

Meaning in plain words: Services that turn the target into a prioritised plan of change.
How this template applies it: Gap analysis, work packages, transition architectures and roadmap.

Core concept (chapter 3): Enterprise Architecture Practice Development Support Services
Meaning in plain words: Services that build and mature the architecture function itself.
How this template applies it: Governance, RACI, maturity targets, and this template as a starter kit.

Meaning in plain words: Deliverables are contracted outputs; artifacts are the models inside them; building blocks are reusable pieces.
How this template applies it: Register rows are artifacts; each chapter is a deliverable; components are building blocks.

Meaning in plain words: Describing the same thing at increasing levels of detail: contextual, conceptual, logical, physical.
How this template applies it: Section 1.5 maps each template artefact to its abstraction level.

Meaning in plain words: The setting: drivers, scope, actors and boundaries, before any design.
How this template applies it: Vision, stakeholders and context diagram.

Meaning in plain words: The main ideas and relationships, free of technology.
How this template applies it: Capability map, conceptual data model, value stream.

Meaning in plain words: A solution-neutral design: components, entities and rules without product choice.
How this template applies it: Layered architecture, data dictionary, interface catalogue.

Meaning in plain words: The concrete implementation: products, platforms, hosting, configuration.
How this template applies it: Technology standards, hosting model, environments.

Meaning in plain words: Short, durable rules that guide decisions, each with rationale and implications.
How this template applies it: The principles register carries 13 principles across four domains.

Meaning in plain words: The ability of systems and organisations to exchange and use information.
How this template applies it: Interface catalogue, exchange standards and integration patterns.

Meaning in plain words: A way to classify architecture assets from generic to specific, and architecture to solution.
How this template applies it: Section 1.2 positions every template artefact on the continuum.

Core concept (chapter 3): TOGAF Content Framework and Enterprise Metamodel
Meaning in plain words: A structure for what architecture content exists and how the pieces relate.
How this template applies it: Section 1.8 and the crosswalk register define our metamodel.

Meaning in plain words: Why content needs a shared structure so views stay consistent.
How this template applies it: Registers use stable IDs and trace columns.

Meaning in plain words: The catalogue of deliverables, artifacts and building blocks across the ADM.
How this template applies it: Chapter 17 lists every artefact and its register.

Meaning in plain words: The entities and relationships used to model an enterprise.
How this template applies it: Entities: capability, process, data entity, component, interface, requirement, risk, work package; links by ID.

Meaning in plain words: Tailoring the metamodel to the organisation's needs.
How this template applies it: Add columns or registers in data/, then extend the stream matrix.

Core concept (chapter 3): Establishing and Maintaining an Enterprise Architecture Capability
Meaning in plain words: Setting up people, process, tools and governance to run architecture continuously.
How this template applies it: Governance chapter, RACI, maturity targets, review cadence.

Core concept (chapter 3): Establishing the Architecture Capability as an Operational Entity
Meaning in plain words: Running architecture as an ongoing service with defined roles, funding and measures.
How this template applies it: Operating model, KPIs and the paperless pipeline.

Core concept (chapter 3): Using the TOGAF Standard with Other Frameworks
Meaning in plain words: Combining TOGAF with BABOK, DAMA-DMBOK, ITIL, ArchiMate and others.
How this template applies it: Crosswalk register aligns TOGAF, BABOK, DMBOK and BA-guild gates.

Core concept (chapter 3): Using the TOGAF Framework with Different Architecture Styles
Meaning in plain words: Applying the framework to styles such as service-oriented, event-driven, cloud-native and agile.
How this template applies it: Section 1.6 covers styles and patterns, with SOA and service orientation.

Meaning in plain words: Views show the architecture to specific stakeholders; viewpoints define how a view is built.
How this template applies it: Section 1.8 lists viewpoints per stakeholder; deck and workbook are views.

Meaning in plain words: Responding to change in small, safe, frequent steps while staying aligned.
How this template applies it: Docs-as-code, incremental transitions and definition of done support agility.

Meaning in plain words: Identifying, assessing and treating risks to architecture work and its outcomes.
How this template applies it: Risk register with likelihood, impact, score and heat map.
